questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish data masking from encryption?
options: Masking hides values from a query's results without changing the stored data; encryption protects data from anyone without the right key, including raw file access
Masking and encryption are two names for the exact same technique
Masking only works on numeric columns, while encryption only works on text columns
Encryption is reversible by anyone, while masking is never reversible
questions.explain: Masking's threat model is a legitimate, authenticated user who shouldn't see a column's true value; encryption protects against someone who doesn't hold the decryption key at all, including at the storage layer.

questions.q: Which T-SQL statement correctly applies Dynamic Data Masking to an existing column, per this lesson?
options: ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN SSN ADD MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'partial(1,"XXX-XX-",4)');
CREATE MASK ON dbo.Customers.SSN;
UPDATE dbo.Customers SET SSN = MASK(SSN);
GRANT MASK ON dbo.Customers TO PUBLIC;
questions.explain: Dynamic Data Masking is applied with ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... ADD MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = ...), directly on the column definition.

questions.q: Which masking function keeps a defined prefix and suffix while replacing the middle of a value?
options: partial()
default()
email()
random()
questions.explain: partial(prefix, padding, suffix) keeps a specified number of characters at the start and end, which is exactly how the lesson's SSN example (partial(1,"XXX-XX-",4)) works.

questions.q: What does the UNMASK permission do?
options: It lets a specific role or user see the real, unmasked value on a column that has a mask defined
It permanently removes the mask from a column for all users
It encrypts the column instead of masking it
It is a synonym for the SELECT permission with no special effect
questions.explain: GRANT UNMASK TO FraudInvestigationRole, as shown in the lesson, lets that specific role bypass the mask and see real values, while everyone else still sees the masked version.

questions.q: According to this lesson and Microsoft's own documentation, what is Dynamic Data Masking's real limit?
options: It's a presentation-layer control meant to limit casual exposure, not a security boundary against a determined, privileged attacker
It makes encryption and tight permissioning completely unnecessary
It physically removes the sensitive data from the database
It can only be applied to a single column per database
questions.explain: A user with enough query access can sometimes infer a masked value indirectly; masking is designed to limit casual, accidental exposure, not replace encryption or RBAC-based permissioning.
